title: Transient triplet blockade in Andreev junction
authors: R. Taranko, J. Baranski, A. Jankiewicz, K. Wrzesniewski, I. Weymann, T. Domanski
abstract: We study the time-dependent triplet configuration, appearing under nonequilibrium conditions in a nanoscopic junction with two quantum dots coupled in series between superconductor and normal metallic lead. We show that in the situation, when both quantum dots are singly occupied by identical spin electrons, the on-dot electron pairing is suppressed what substantially affects the subgap charge transport. We investigate processes in which such configuration can be temporarily encountered, either due to the initial conditions or by imposing the external magnetic field. Our analytical and numerical calculations provide estimations for the temporal scales, characterizing evolution of the triplet configuration which could be manifested in the time-resolved tunneling measurements. Such nonequilibrium features of the triplet configuration might be relevant to operations on superconducting qubits, in their conventional and/or topological realizations.
summary: The paper theoretically models charge transport through a double quantum dot junction coupled to superconductors, focusing on transient blockade effects caused by spin triplet configurations. By analyzing time evolution under magnetic fields and bias voltages, the authors characterize how these non-equilibrium states suppress Andreev current and how external stimuli can restore superconducting coherence.
main_problem: The study investigates transient triplet blockade effects arising from non-equilibrium conditions within a double quantum dot junction coupled to superconductors.
main_result: The system exhibits distinct time scales for charge transfer in weakly coupled regimes, and the superconducting pairing amplitude shows a non-monotonic dependence on an external magnetic field due to bound state energy rearrangement.
method: The analysis employs analytical and numerical techniques based on the Heisenberg equation of motion and Laplace transforms to track time-dependent expectation values of operators.
model_or_system: The physical system is a nanoscopic junction comprising two quantum dots (QD1, QD2) coupled in series between a normal metal lead (N) and a superconductor (S). The model incorporates Anderson-type Hamiltonians for the QDs and BCS theory for the superconductor.
key_observables: Time-dependent electron occupancy ($n_{j\sigma}(t)$), on-dot pairing amplitudes ($\chi_{jj}(t)$), and charge currents ($j_{N\sigma}, j_S$).
important_parameters: Inter-dot coupling strength ($V_{12}$), external magnetic field ($B$), bias voltage ($V$), and characteristic time scales ($	au \sim \hbar/\Gamma_N$ vs $	au_A \sim \hbar/|V_{12}|$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes the large bandwidth limit for the normal lead and sometimes neglects correlation effects initially, though advanced methods like tdNRG are referenced.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate time-dependent charge currents showing suppression upon magnetic field switching and recovery with bias, and show the evolution of pairing and spin correlations under varying fields and couplings.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the Hamiltonian, deriving equations for time-dependent observables using Green's functions/Laplace transforms, analyzing specific physical protocols (initial quench, B-field application, voltage bias), and comparing results across different coupling regimes (strong vs. weak).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium dynamics in superconducting quantum circuits, which is crucial for understanding energy dissipation and coherence control in solid-state qubits.
